question_text: Find the eccentricity, coordinates of foci, length of latus rectum and equations of directrices of the ellipse 9x² + 16y² − 36x + 32y − 92 = 0.

insider_note: Completing the square turns this into the standard ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 moved to the centre (2, −1) — so the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum come straight from a = 4, b = 3 and need no re-deriving; only the foci and the directrices need the centre added in, because those are positions, not lengths.

steps.label: Complete the square to standard form
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own, but this is the real extra work here compared with an ellipse already given in standard form.
steps.memory_tip: Group the x-terms and y-terms separately before completing each square.

lines.text: 9 and 16, and move −92 to the right:

lines: a > b, so the major axis is horizontal.
steps.why: Completing the square in x and y turns the general equation into the shifted standard form (x − h)²/a² + (y − k)²/b² = 1, which reads off the same a² = 16, b² = 9 as the centred ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, but centred at (h, k) = (2, −1).
common_mistakes: Adding 4 and 1 (the numbers needed inside each bracket) but forgetting to also add 9·4 and 16·1 on the right-hand side.
Losing the sign of k when reading (y − k)² — here y + 1 means k = −1, not +1.

steps.label: Eccentricity
steps.margin_note: First mark. a² = 16, b² = 9, a > b, centre (h, k) = (2, −1) — the same a and b as x²/16 + y²/9 = 1.
steps.memory_tip: The eccentricity never depends on where the centre is — only on a and b.
steps.why: Shifting the centre never changes the shape of the ellipse, so a, b and e are identical to an ellipse of the same a² and b² centred at the origin.
common_mistakes: Trying to fold the centre (2, −1) into the eccentricity formula — it has no effect on e.
Leaving a² in the denominator instead of a.

steps.label: Foci
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Shift both foci by the centre (2, −1); the y-coordinate stays −1 for a horizontal ellipse.

lines.text: The foci are on the major axis, a distance ae

steps.why: For a horizontal ellipse centred at (h, k), the foci move ae to the right and left of the centre along the line y = k.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to shift the y-coordinate to −1 and leaving it at 0.
Adding ae to k instead of h.

steps.label: Length of latus rectum
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Identical to the centred ellipse — the centre shift never changes a length.
steps.memory_tip: Latus rectum equals 2 times the smaller square, over the bigger axis length.

lines.text: The latus rectum is the chord through a focus,

steps.why: The latus rectum is a length, and lengths are unchanged by shifting the centre — only positions move.
common_mistakes: Trying to add the centre coordinates into a length calculation.

steps.label: Equations of directrices
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Shift x = h ± a/e, and multiply through by √7 to clear the fraction.
steps.memory_tip: Directrices use a/e from the shifted centre x = h, not from the origin.

steps.why: Each directrix shifts by the same h as the centre, so x = h ± a/e replaces x = ±a/e once the ellipse is off-centre.
common_mistakes: Using x = ±a/e without adding the centre's x-coordinate h = 2.
Multiplying only the a/e term by √7 and forgetting to multiply the shifted 2 as well.
